assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Bundle construction with a completeness oracle.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the bundle's manifest entry count equals the extracted blob count; (2) the dependency closure of every included package is fully contained in the bundle, computed independently by the resolver — a bundle missing a transitive dependency is unusable offline and must fail export.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: An import path that trusts its input is the classic supply-chain hole.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a bundle with a tampered blob is rejected at import, naming the entry; (2) an index census before and after confirms zero entries changed on the rejected import — a partial import that then rejects is still a compromise.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement import of an offline bundle: re-verify every signature and digest against the local trust policy (never trust the bundle's own claim), and define what happens when an imported version already exists locally with a different digest — a collision must be surfaced, never silently overwritten.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Fairness properties (both sides recorded, no silent deletion) are design judgement.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a full report-then-dispute-then-resolve cycle produces the expected event sequence; (2) an attempt to delete or edit a prior record is refused and the refusal itself is logged. Append-only must be enforced, not merely intended.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Policy-as-code design; the failure mode is a document nobody enforces.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) every (role, action) pair is evaluated and matches the policy table; (2) a docs-versus-policy parity check proving the governance markdown and the machine-readable policy declare the same permissions — a mismatch in either direction fails the unit.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: An irreversible external action is exactly what this guard exists to prevent.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) every enumerated publishing entry point returns BLOCKED-NEEDS-OWNER under PR-ONLY; (2) a static audit proving no outbound publish call exists outside the guarded module, so the guard cannot be bypassed by calling a lower layer directly.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Composition of existing checks with a report-shape oracle.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the linter's finding set over the known-bad fixture package; (2) each composed sub-check run standalone over the same fixture, requiring the union to equal the linter's set — a composition that silently drops a sub-check is the defect this catches.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Referential-integrity checking is an exact algorithm.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the linter's findings over an index with one planted defect of each class; (2) an independent recomputation of the reference graph confirming the same dangling and orphan sets. assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: The CLI is where an irreversible external action would be triggered; the safe path must be the default path.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: CI wiring with a red/green oracle on a fixture PR.

work_units.title: Test fixture marketplace: a synthetic known-good registry

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Designing fixtures that genuinely exercise a defect (rather than merely being labelled bad) is adversarial judgement.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a coverage matrix proving every fixture has exactly one gate that fires on it; (2) a cross-check proving no fixture is silently passed by ALL gates, and that the good fixtures from IMP-0118 are passed by all of them in the same run. Both directions of the both-states test are required.
work_units.question_or_target: Build the deliberately-bad companion corpus — a package with a bad signature, one with a digest mismatch, one carrying a synthetic secret, one containing a .git directory, one declaring excessive permissions, one with a path-traversal entry name, one with a dependency cycle, one with an invalid SPDX id — and assert that every corresponding gate fires on its own fixture.
work_units.retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Cross-vendor adversarial reviewer must add one fixture class the implementer did not think of and report whether any gate catches it.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_adversarial_fixtures.py::test_every_bad_fixture_trips_its_gate
tools/marketplace/tests/test_adversarial_fixtures.py::test_no_good_fixture_trips_any_gate
the synthetic secret must be provably synthetic (a documented non-credential) and must never be a real token
work_units.title: Adversarial fixture set: the negative controls every gate must fire on

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: A bidirectional set comparison plus command execution; exact algorithm.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the declared-minus-documented and documented-minus-declared sets, both required empty; (2) every documented command actually executed in its documented form with the documented exit behaviour — a documented command that does not run is a docs-code disagreement the set check cannot see.
work_units.question_or_target: Enforce, in both directions, that every command, skill and hook a package declares has documentation, and that every documented command actually exists and runs — closing the program stopping condition 'docs and code agree' at the package level rather than as a final-report assertion.
work_units.retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must run three documented commands verbatim from the docs and report any that fail.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_docs_parity.py::test_both_direction_sets_are_empty
tools/marketplace/tests/test_docs_commands_run.py::test_every_documented_command_executes
NEGATIVE CONTROL: remove one doc entry and assert the parity test names exactly that command
work_units.title: Package documentation parity gate (declared surface versus documented surface)

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Content addressing plus refcounting with exact equality oracles.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) storing the same blob twice yields one on-disk object, verified by directory listing; (2) on read, the recomputed digest equals the key, so a silently corrupted object is detected rather than served. Deduplication without read verification trades one failure mode for another.
inputs: IMP-0040 plugin cache (a different layer: runtime artefacts, not package blobs)
work_units.question_or_target: Store package blobs by digest in a single local store so an identical blob referenced by several versions or collections is stored once, with reference counting that makes deletion safe, and with verification on read.
work_units.retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must confirm the refcount survives a crash (it must be derivable from the index, not held only in memory).
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_blob_store.py::test_dedupe_and_refcount
tools/marketplace/tests/test_blob_store.py::test_corrupted_object_is_detected_on_read
NEGATIVE CONTROL: deleting a blob still referenced must be refused
work_units.title: Content-addressed package blob store shared across installs

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Backoff behaviour is measurable against a fake server with an exact timing oracle.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) against a fake server returning 429 with Retry-After, the observed inter-request intervals match the declared policy within tolerance; (2) the request arrival histogram for a 50-item batch shows staggering rather than a single burst, measured server-side. Client-side intent is not evidence of server-side arrival shape.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the network client so a batch of installs staggers its arrivals, honours Retry-After, backs off exponentially with jitter, and surfaces a 429 storm as a named condition rather than as a cascade of individual failures — treating arrival rate as a scheduler input per the scaling doctrine.
work_units.retry_policy: the unit's own policy under test; implementation retries are bounded exponential with jitter, max 5, then a named 429-storm condition
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must confirm jitter is genuinely random and not a fixed offset that re-synchronises the herd.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_rate_limit_client.py::test_retry_after_is_honoured
tools/marketplace/tests/test_rate_limit_client.py::test_batch_arrivals_are_staggered
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a client without staggering must produce a burst histogram, proving the measurement discriminates
work_units.title: Rate-limit-aware registry client with jittered arrival staggering

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Scheduled re-hashing with an exact comparison.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a deliberately mutated blob is identified by the sweep, naming the entry; (2) the sweep's coverage count equals the store's object count, proving it examined everything rather than sampling. A clean sweep with an unverified coverage count is not a clean bill of health.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement a periodic sweep that re-verifies every stored blob against its recorded digest and every index entry against its blob, reporting drift with the affected entries named — bit rot and out-of-band edits are only detectable by re-measurement, never by the original write succeeding.
work_units.retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must confirm the sweep is bounded in runtime and cannot itself become the resource-pressure source.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_integrity_sweep.py::test_mutated_blob_is_named
tools/marketplace/tests/test_integrity_sweep.py::test_coverage_equals_object_count
NEGATIVE CONTROL: an untouched store reports zero drift in the same run
work_units.title: Scheduled integrity audit sweep over stored blobs and index digests

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: A restore path that has never been rehearsed is a claim, not a capability.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the restored registry passes the index linter with zero findings; (2) a functional probe (resolve, install, verify one package) succeeds against the restored copy. Structural validity and functional equivalence are different claims and both are required.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement backup and restore for the index, blob store and event log, and script a drill that restores into a scratch location and proves the restored registry is functionally equivalent. Restoring over a live registry is destructive and owner-gated.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry on a restore against a live target
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must perform the drill themselves from the documented runbook alone.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_registry_dr.py::test_restore_is_lint_clean_and_functional
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a backup missing the blob store must fail the functional probe, proving it discriminates
restore into a scratch path must never write to the live registry (census assertion)
work_units.title: Registry backup, restore, and a rehearsed disaster-recovery drill

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: A GC that miscounts references deletes live data; the estate's rule is that content preservation must be PROVEN before deletion.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals per candidate: (1) zero references found by the index/lockfile scan; (2) zero references found by an independently written reachability walk from the deploy provenance ledger. A candidate must be unreferenced under BOTH to be deletable; disagreement means keep.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement a GC that deletes only objects proven unreferenced by the index, the lockfiles, and the deploy provenance ledger, with a mandatory dry-run listing every candidate and its zero-reference proof before anything is removed. Deletion is owner-gated.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry on a deletion path
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must construct a reference the implementer's scan does not know about and confirm the second walk catches it, or that the GC keeps the object.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_gc.py::test_referenced_blob_is_never_collected
tools/marketplace/tests/test_gc.py::test_dry_run_lists_every_candidate_with_its_proof
NEGATIVE CONTROL: plant a reference only in a lockfile and assert the blob survives
work_units.title: Garbage collection for unreferenced blobs and dangling deploy targets

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Set intersection across projection maps; exact algorithm.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the intersection of the two packages' projected path sets is non-empty and is named; (2) an actual sequential install of both into a throwaway HOME, with a census proving the first package's file would have been overwritten had the guard not fired. The second signal is what proves the conflict is real rather than theoretical.
work_units.question_or_target: Detect, before install and at index-lint time, when two packages would deploy to the same live path, and refuse the install with both claimants named — so the second install cannot silently overwrite the first package's file.
work_units.retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must confirm the detector uses the same casefold normalisation as IMP-0022, not a separate rule.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_path_conflict.py::test_conflicting_pair_is_refused
NEGATIVE CONTROL: two disjoint packages install together in the same run
casefold conflicts must also be detected (README.md vs readme.md across packages)
work_units.title: Cross-package deploy-path conflict detector

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: The whole anti-duplicate-control-plane constraint reduces to getting this boundary right.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a schema-validated handoff object flows end to end and the resulting install matches the direct-install census; (2) a structural audit counting file-placement call sites across both modules and requiring exactly one. A planted second call site must make the audit fail.

work_units.retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must attempt to install by calling the plugin installer directly and confirm the transaction id requirement makes the bypass visible.

tools/marketplace/tests/test_handoff_contract.py::test_handoff_object_validates_and_installs
NEGATIVE CONTROL: add a second placement path and assert the audit catches it
work_units.title: Typed registry-to-plugin handoff contract (one installer control plane)

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Must integrate with a live monitor on the owner's machine without disturbing the existing panes.

work_units.evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the new pane renders with live values, confirmed by launching the cockpit; (2) the same values queried directly from the registry APIs match what the pane displays, so the pane is not showing a cached or fabricated number. Additionally the pre-existing panes must still render, verified by count.

work_units.retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot
work_units.reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must launch the cockpit and confirm no existing pane regressed, since the cockpit is a live owner-facing surface.
tests_required: tools/marketplace/tests/test_cockpit_pane.py::test_pane_values_match_direct_query
REGRESSION: the existing cockpit panes still render (count and content unchanged)

Acceptance: the diff is DIRECTIONAL and reports both sides' unique content, because a one-directional read cannot see two-directional divergence - the measured failure mode that produced 31 data-loss-pointing misclassifications on this estate.

antisymmetry check computed over the fixture matrix
work_units.title: Implement semantic diff of two workflows over aligned stages, roles and gates

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) reconstruction equals the pre-collapse set exactly; (2) rank is computed from independent evidence and decision impact, NOT from how many sources repeated the idea (assert the count field is absent from the ranking function's inputs).

work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: pre-collapse set reconstructible from the graph (set equality)
ranking function does not read repetition count (AST/param assertion)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) orphan-component count == 0 (computed); (2) a planted orphan makes the build fail (detector control).

work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) cell coverage == |components|^2 (computed); (2) every FORBIDDEN cell carries a machine-readable reason drawn from a closed set.
work_units.question_or_target: Question: for each ordered component pair, may they compose, and under what precondition? Target: compute the map from contracts (output type, tool policy, licence, stop-rule compatibility). Acceptance: the map is exhaustive over the component set (no missing cells) and each FORBIDDEN cell names its reason.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: cell coverage complete (computed, no missing pairs)

work_units.title: Build the merge/compatibility map: which components may legally and technically compose

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) a synthetic contradictory pair is flagged; (2) a superficially similar but compatible pair is NOT flagged (false-positive control).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: detect pairs whose contracts CONFLICT even though both are individually valid - e.g. one requires unanimity, the other forbids it; one needs egress, the other declares an air-gapped policy. Acceptance: conflicts are detected structurally from the predicate trees, not by keyword matching on prose.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: contradictory pair flagged; compatible look-alike not flagged (both-states)
detection reads the predicate tree, not the prose (AST assertion)
work_units.title: Implement component conflict detection (contradictory stop rules, incompatible tool policy)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) vectors computed for 100% of registry candidates; (2) an unversioned taxonomy edit fails the guard (detector control).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: express what each workflow can DO as a vector over a declared capability taxonomy, so coverage is comparable and gaps are computable. Acceptance: the taxonomy is declared once and versioned; adding a capability without a version bump fails a guard.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: coverage vectors computed for every candidate (no nulls)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) the parser recounts the categories from the spec text and sums to 96 without a hardcoded constant; (2) a deliberately removed category changes the sum (detector fires).
work_units.question_or_target: Question: which of the library categories the spec mandates (research/evidence 15, engineering/reliability 21, security/governance 12, product/design 15, data/science 16, collective-intelligence/meta 17 = 96 exactly, counted from _USER-PROMPTS.md:10902-10907) have ZERO covering candidate? Target: compute the gap set. Acceptance: the tool reproduces the 96 total independently from the spec text - a hardcoded 96 is a broken detector.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: category counts derived from spec text, not hardcoded (sum == 96)
removing a category from the fixture changes the computed sum
work_units.title: Implement the coverage-gap finder against the required library taxonomy

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) lineage present after export/import round trip (field-by-field equality); (2) a lineage-stripped fixture is REFUSED by the publish path.
work_units.question_or_target: Target: record, for every generated or fused workflow, the exact source components, their versions, their licences and the fusion strategy used. Acceptance: lineage survives a round trip through export/import - 'workflow provenance or license is lost' is a named failure class and must be impossible, not merely avoided.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: lineage survives round trip (computed equality)
lineage-stripped workflow refused at publish (both-states)
work_units.title: Build the lineage graph linking every fused workflow to its source components

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) 8/8 strategies pass the inverse property; (2) a deliberately lossy fusion fails the inverse test (detector fires on the broken state).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: implement decompose(fusion) -> source components and prove it is a true inverse of the fusion operation for every strategy. Acceptance: for each of the eight fusion strategies, decompose(fuse(a,b)) yields components equal to {a,b} under the structural fingerprint - eight separate assertions, not one generic claim.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: 8/8 fusion strategies satisfy the decomposition inverse
planted lossy fusion must fail the inverse test
work_units.title: Implement decomposition: turn a fusion back into its source components, and test the inverse

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) a planted renamed copy is excluded; (2) a genuinely distinct sibling with similar naming is NOT excluded (false-positive control).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: detect renamed copies and trivial forks and EXCLUDE them from the 160-candidate floor. Acceptance: the floor count is reported twice - raw and de-forked - and the de-forked number is the one that counts, because the spec explicitly forbids counting trivial forks or renamed copies (10725).
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: planted renamed copy excluded; similar-name distinct sibling retained (both-states)
raw and de-forked counts both reported
work_units.title: Implement the trivial-fork detector so renamed copies cannot inflate the candidate count

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) contract-mismatch fixture refused; (2) a valid splice runs end to end on the fake rail and its plan differs from both parents (proving it is not silently one parent).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: implement the stage-splice strategy - replace one workflow's stage with a better-performing stage from another, preserving the surrounding contract. Acceptance: the spliced stage's input/output contract is checked against its neighbours BEFORE the fusion is emitted; a contract mismatch is a refusal.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
work_units.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: contract mismatch refused (both-states: matching contract accepted)
spliced plan differs from BOTH parents (computed, guards against no-op fusion)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) core+delta reproduces each source (n/n fingerprint equality); (2) an over-eager core that loses a source stage fails that equality (detector fires).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: extract the intersection of two or more workflows as a reusable core and re-express each source as core + delta. Acceptance: re-composing core+delta reproduces each source exactly (fingerprint equality) - otherwise the 'core' is a lossy summary masquerading as a factorization.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
work_units.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: core + delta reproduces every source exactly
planted lossy core must fail reproduction
work_units.title: Implement common-core fusion

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) union(w,w) == w by fingerprint; (2) union(a,b) contains every capability of a and of b (coverage-vector superset, computed).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: union two workflows, collapsing structurally identical stages rather than concatenating them. Acceptance: the union of a workflow with ITSELF is that workflow (idempotence), which is the cheapest possible falsifier of a naive concatenating implementation.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: idempotence: union(w,w) == w
capability superset property holds for both parents

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) 100% of chosen stages carry a benchmark run id; (2) forcing a no-evidence stage into the input makes the build fail (detector control).
work_units.question_or_target: Question: for each stage slot, which source's implementation actually performs best on matched cases? Target: select per-stage by measured evidence, not by reputation. Acceptance: the selection record cites the benchmark run id for every chosen stage; a stage chosen with no evidence is a build failure.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: every chosen stage cites a benchmark run id

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) static reachability shows 0 unreachable branches; (2) a planted unreachable branch is detected (detector control).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: emit a fusion that dispatches to different source sub-workflows based on a typed runtime predicate. Acceptance: every branch is reachable (static reachability proof) and the default branch is explicit - an unreachable branch is dead capability masquerading as coverage.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: 0 unreachable branches (computed)
planted unreachable branch is detected

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) a correlated-members fixture is flagged as non-independent; (2) an independent-members fixture is not flagged (false-positive control).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: run N source workflows and aggregate. Acceptance: the aggregation rule is declared and typed (majority | weighted | evidence-gated | execution-consensus), and an ensemble that agrees only because its members share an input is flagged - correlated members are not independent evidence, which is the measured failure of counting agents instead of probes.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) correctness delta vs the expensive form computed on matched cases; (2) work reduction computed from the budget ledger, not estimated.
work_units.question_or_target: Target: compose a cheap fast source and an expensive thorough source into a progressive workflow with an explicit escalation predicate. Acceptance: on the benchmark set the progressive form must match the expensive form's correctness within a declared tolerance while doing measurably less work - both numbers reported, and a failure to meet either is a REJECT not a caveat.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
work_units.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: correctness within declared tolerance AND measured work reduction (both required)
a progressive form that never escalates on a hard case must FAIL (both-states)
work_units.title: Implement progressive fusion (cheap tier first, escalate only on need)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) budget sum equality computed from the ledger; (2) a child failure under a `continue` policy leaves siblings running (observed in the event log, not inferred).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: compose workflows as first-class units via the Subworkflow node, with budget and failure policy rolled up. Acceptance: a two-level meta-workflow's total budget equals the sum of its children (no double-count, asserted against the immutable budget ledger) and a child failure maps to the parent's declared policy rather than aborting the whole tree by default.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
work_units.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: budget roll-up has no double count (ledger assertion)
child failure honours the parent policy (both-states: abort vs continue)
work_units.title: Implement meta-workflow composition (a workflow whose units are workflows)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) a bigger-but-not-better fusion is rejected by the gate; (2) a genuinely complementary fusion passes on the capability-vector criterion with the new capability named.
work_units.question_or_target: Target: no fusion enters the library unless it beats its sources on a declared metric OR provides a capability none of them has. Acceptance: a fusion that is merely LARGER is rejected - 'a merged workflow is not accepted because it contains more stages' (11170) is implemented as a gate, not repeated as advice.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
work_units.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: bigger-but-not-better fusion REJECTED (both-states: a better one passes)
complementarity is proven by a capability-vector difference, not by prose
work_units.title: Implement the fusion admission gate: outperform or materially complement, or be rejected

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) set-difference == empty on all admitted fusions; (2) a planted dropped stage makes the detector fire (both-states control).
work_units.question_or_target: Target: assert that a fusion retains every capability of every source. Acceptance: the check is a computed set difference over capability vectors and it FIRES on a planted loss - 'workflow fusion loses a source capability' is a named failure class (11333).
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: capability set difference empty for all admitted fusions

Target: an AST-level detector modelled on tools/agentrail/tests/test_no_rival_core.py, applied to every generated artifact. Acceptance: it fires on a planted rival oracle; the hard constraint at 10483 becomes mechanical rather than aspirational.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: planted rival oracle detected (detector fires on the broken state)

work_units.title: Implement the duplicate-control-plane detector for fusions and imports

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) a goal already covered by the library returns the existing workflow, not a new one; (2) an uncovered goal produces a schema-valid workflow that passes static validation.
work_units.question_or_target: Target: given a typed goal + constraints, emit a schema-valid Workflow. Acceptance: generation is gated by the scout - if an existing workflow already covers the goal, the generator must REFUSE and return the existing one, because 'workflow discovery ignores an existing superior workflow and rebuilds it' is a named failure class (11331).
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: covered goal returns the incumbent (both-states: uncovered goal generates)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) trace replay outcome equality; (2) the cited gap is absent from a fresh gap-finder run (re-measured, not asserted).

Acceptance: a trace-derived workflow REPLAYS the trace's outcome on the same inputs, and a gap-derived workflow closes the specific gap it cites - each verified by re-running the gap finder afterwards and showing that gap absent.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: trace-derived workflow reproduces the trace outcome
gap-derived workflow removes the cited gap on re-measurement (both-states)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) an unreachable-barrier fixture is rejected while the reachable twin passes; (2) the reachability set is computed by graph traversal and cross-checked against an independent topological sort (two derivations of the same set).

Acceptance: a workflow whose barrier awaits a unit outside every path is REJECTED before dispatch - today validate.py catches barrier-awaits-unknown but not barrier-awaits-unreachable, which is a different defect.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv

tests_required: unreachable barrier rejected; reachable twin accepted (both-states)

Target: a static analysis that answers it for the Loop x Barrier x Subworkflow combinations. Acceptance: a mutual-wait fixture is detected statically, and 'one hung unit blocks a large batch' (11318) is unrepresentable when per-unit pipelines are declared.

work_units.title: Implement deadlock and livelock analysis over Loop and Barrier combinations

Acceptance: a simulated run makes zero network calls and zero real spawns, and the simulator refuses to run a workflow that requires a capability the fake rail cannot honestly emulate - a silently faked capability is worse than a refusal.

Acceptance: the ranking is computed from pairwise results with ties reported as ties - a forced total order over statistically indistinguishable candidates is a fabricated verdict.

tests_required: injected tie is reported as a tie (both-states with a clear winner)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) a cross-corpus comparison is refused with a named reason; (2) a same-corpus comparison produces a delta computed from stored per-case rows, not from a stored summary.

work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer; must confirm the inversion against the instrument, not against the prose
work_units.tests_required: both-states test: a fixture rule with no frontmatter must resolve ALWAYS-ON and the same file WITH paths:["**/*"] must resolve LAZY. A resolver that returns the same answer for both fails.
work_units.title: Frontmatter load-semantics resolver (always-on vs path-scoped)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Ranked confusability table (top 20 pairs) with the token-overlap score and both descriptions quoted; plus the exact count of zero-negative-scope capabilities with ids listed.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement tools/router/desc_lint.py scoring every capability description on four axes: trigger enumeration, explicit negative scope (a do-NOT-use-for clause), disambiguation against its nearest sibling, and vocabulary that is enumerated rather than a bare tag name. Exact question: how many of the indexed capabilities have ZERO negative-scope clause, and which pair of capabilities is most confusable by description alone?
work_units.retry_policy: max 3 attempts for transient provider 429/529 only; zero retries on a schema-invalid report
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus a cross-vendor codex critic on the top-5 confusable pairs only
work_units.tests_required: planted-mutant control: rename one capability and rewrite its description as a paraphrase of a sibling; the linter must surface that pair in the top 5 confusable pairs.
work_units.title: Routing-description quality linter with negative-scope coverage

work_units.evidence_requirement: For a 60-query labelled corpus, a per-query trace naming the fired row id; and at least 8 queries where the correct answer is the empty set and the stage returns empty.
work_units.failure_classification: P2-degraded / classes: use-vs-mention (matching payload text instead of semantic role), always-fires-default
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the deterministic first stage: a trigger table matching on literal keyword, glob path, cwd prefix, and tool-verb, with NO model call. Exact target: every selection this stage makes must be explainable by naming the exact table row that fired, and the stage must be able to return the empty set.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s; two-strikes pivot to a table-driven rewrite
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer; must verify the empty-set path is reachable and not swallowed by a default
work_units.tests_required: unit per matcher kind (keyword/glob/cwd/verb); negative control: 8 no-fit queries must yield zero rows, and a mutation that deletes one trigger row must turn exactly one labelled query red.
work_units.title: Deterministic rule-based matcher (first-stage router)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Recall@5 on the planted-mutant paraphrase set for lexical vs semantic, same control set, same seed; plus the exact pinned model id and digest.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the second-stage semantic matcher over capability descriptions using a version-PINNED local embedding model, with a documented offline fallback when the model is unavailable. Exact question: does the semantic stage recover the paraphrase pairs that the lexical linter provably cannot, measured on the planted-mutant set from IMP-0388?
work_units.retry_policy: max 3 attempts for model-fetch transients; zero retries on a nondeterministic ranking - that is a design defect
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-codex-reviewer, fresh context, must re-run the recall measurement
work_units.tests_required: determinism test: same query + same pinned model + same seed yields byte-identical ranking twice. Offline test: with the model absent, the matcher must degrade LOUDLY (typed DEGRADED result), never silently return lexical results labelled as semantic.
work_units.title: Semantic matcher with pinned local embedding model and offline fallback

work_units.evidence_requirement: A reliability diagram (bin, predicted confidence, observed accuracy, n) over the labelled corpus, with the Brier score; any bin whose observed accuracy is outside its band by more than 0.15 must be named.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement reciprocal-rank fusion of the deterministic and semantic stages and attach a CALIBRATED confidence to each returned capability. Exact question: on the labelled corpus, is the reported confidence calibrated - does the 0.9 band actually contain about 90 percent correct selections - or is it an uncalibrated score being displayed as a probability?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; a second uncalibrated result escalates - do not tune weights a third time without a fresh-context re-derivation
work_units.reviewer_requirement: 2 independent reviewers: a correctness reviewer and an adversarial refuter who defaults to REFUTED on insufficient evidence
work_units.tests_required: calibration regression: a deliberately miscalibrated fusion weight must move at least one bin outside tolerance and turn the test red (mutation control).
work_units.title: Rank fusion and confidence calibration across the two matcher stages

work_units.evidence_requirement: Measured injected-token count for the 40-above-threshold adversarial case, taken from a real tokenizer count of the emitted payload, not from an estimate.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the injection budgeter: a per-capability token-cost model, a hard total ceiling, and a refusal to inject past it. Exact target: reproduce and then prevent the measured skills-context-budget overflow that was the root cause of naive-session behavior, and prove the ceiling holds when 40 capabilities all score above threshold.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s; two-strikes pivot to a hard truncation strategy
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer; must confirm the counter is not mutated inside a subshell
work_units.tests_required: ceiling test at k=40 must cap; a mutation raising the ceiling constant must turn the test red. Explicit test that the cap is enforced in the MAIN shell, not inside a command substitution where a counter mutation would be lost.
work_units.title: Top-k injection budgeter with a hard context-flood ceiling

work_units.evidence_requirement: Full list of duplicated capability names with both candidate paths, the winner, and the rule that decided it; plus a same-input-different-cwd determinism check.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement conflict resolution for a capability name that resolves to more than one record: directory-scoped versus unscoped variants, and the same skill present in two duplicated deployed trees. Exact question: for every duplicated name in the index, which record wins, and is the winner deterministic across two runs from different cwds?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; escalate on any nondeterministic winner
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer; must check the two duplicated deployed trees specifically
work_units.tests_required: fixture with a scoped and an unscoped variant of one name; assert most-specific wins from inside the scoped directory and unscoped wins outside it. Negative control: a name with no duplicate must not enter the resolution path at all.
work_units.title: Capability conflict resolution with most-specific-scope-wins

work_units.evidence_requirement: A precedence table with a worked example per level, and a demonstration that a banned capability scoring 0.99 is still excluded.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the override layer so the owner can pin a capability always-on, ban one outright, and set per-project overrides, with an explicit precedence order. Exact target: an owner ban must beat every score the router can produce, and the precedence order must be printed, not implied.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; an override bug silently disables owner control
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus owner-visible read of the precedence table
work_units.tests_required: ban-beats-score test; pin-survives-budget test (a pinned capability must not be dropped by the IMP-0392 ceiling); per-project override must not leak into a sibling project (session/project keying).
work_units.title: User override layer: pin, ban, and per-project precedence

work_units.evidence_requirement: Three worked explanations from the labelled corpus, each independently reconstructed by a reviewer who was given only the explanation and the index.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the explanation record: for each selection, why this capability, which rule or score produced it, and which capabilities were near-misses that did NOT make the cut. Exact question: can an owner reading only the explanation reconstruct the decision without re-running the router?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer performs the blind reconstruction
work_units.tests_required: reconstruction test: a script consuming only the explanation must reproduce the selected set exactly; if it cannot, the explanation is incomplete and the test fails.
work_units.title: Selection-explanation emitter with near-miss disclosure

work_units.evidence_requirement: Terminal-state audit: for 100 random queries, assert 100 terminal verdicts and zero empty or null returns.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the no-fit path so the router emits an explicit typed NO-CAPABILITY-FITS verdict with the closest rejected candidates, rather than injecting a weak match. Exact target: silence must be impossible - every route call returns a terminal state, either a selection or an explicit no-fit.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; two-strikes pivot
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer; must attempt to construct a query that returns neither a selection nor a no-fit
work_units.tests_required: no-fit corpus must all return NO-CAPABILITY-FITS; a mutation lowering the threshold so a weak match is injected must turn the test red.
work_units.title: Explicit NO-CAPABILITY-FITS terminal verdict

work_units.evidence_requirement: Breadth figure with its denominator stated (offered / total indexed), and the join key named; any record that could carry a path outside the estate must be shown scrubbed.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement privacy-scrubbed router telemetry recording which capabilities were offered, which were used, and the eventual task outcome, joined on a session-scoped key. Exact question: what fraction of the indexed repertoire is ever offered in a month, and does offering a capability correlate with task success?
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry on a scrub failure - that is a disclosure risk, escalate immediately
work_units.reviewer_requirement: cross-vendor-codex-reviewer plus a claude privacy reviewer; both must PASS
work_units.tests_required: scrub test: a planted secret-shaped token and a planted absolute user path must both be absent from the emitted telemetry (negative control on the scrubber).
work_units.title: Router telemetry: capability-breadth and task-success join

work_units.evidence_requirement: Corpus size, negative-query fraction, and the measured score of an always-top-3 baseline on it; if that baseline scores well the corpus is too easy and must be rebuilt.
work_units.question_or_target: Build the labelled router regression corpus: query, expected capability set, and rationale - with at least 25 percent NEGATIVE queries whose expected set is empty. Exact target: a corpus that cannot be satisfied by a router that always returns the top-3 most popular capabilities.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; if the baseline still scores well after 2, redesign the corpus rather than re-tune
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer relabels a random 10 percent blind and must agree at kappa >= 0.7
work_units.tests_required: baseline-defeat test: the always-top-3 stub must score below the declared floor. Corpus schema test.
work_units.title: Router regression corpus with mandatory negative queries

work_units.evidence_requirement: Mutation table: mutation, expected red, observed result, and for every survivor the exact behavior left unprotected. A suite that stays green on all four is a broken detector, not a passing suite.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the router mutation harness: programmatically corrupt one description, delete one trigger row, invert one precedence rule, and unpin the embedding model - and assert the regression suite goes RED for each. Exact question: how many of the four mutations SURVIVE the suite, and what exactly is unprotected for each survivor?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; a harness that reports zero mutations caught is a detector failure - fix the harness before re-running
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter who defaults to REFUTED; must attempt a fifth mutation of their own design
work_units.tests_required: the harness itself needs a control: one mutation known to be caught must be caught, proving the harness can observe redness at all.
work_units.title: Router mutation harness proving the regression suite detects what it claims

work_units.evidence_requirement: Paired comparison on identical queries with confidence intervals; the baseline must be captured BEFORE the router is armed, not reconstructed afterwards.
work_units.question_or_target: Measure the new router against the CURRENT live selection behavior on the same corpus: precision@k, recall of relevant capabilities, and repertoire breadth. Exact question: does the new router beat the live baseline on breadth WITHOUT losing precision, and if it trades one for the other, by exactly how much?
work_units.retry_policy: max 3 attempts for provider transients only
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-codex-reviewer re-runs the benchmark from the receipt alone
work_units.tests_required: benchmark determinism: two runs on the same frozen corpus and pinned model must agree within the declared tolerance.
work_units.title: Router-versus-live-baseline benchmark on breadth and precision

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two disjoint lists (repo-only, live-only) with counts, produced by set difference over capability_id - a mechanical comparison, not a judgement call.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the detector for spec failure class 'skill exists in repo but not in live skill directory' as a ROUTER-visible defect: the index must flag any capability the router could select that cannot actually load. Exact question: how many indexed capabilities are repo-only, and how many are live-only?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-computes the set difference independently
work_units.tests_required: detector control: plant one repo-only and one live-only fixture capability; both must appear. A capability present in both must NOT appear.
work_units.title: Repo-versus-live capability presence gap detector

work_units.evidence_requirement: Timed edit-then-query trace showing the changed answer, plus the observed behavior on a deliberately truncated and a deliberately zero-byte cache file.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement cache invalidation for the capability index using content hash plus mtime, with an explicit corrupted-cache recovery path. Exact target: editing a capability description must change the router's answer on the very next call, and a truncated cache file must trigger a rebuild rather than a crash or a silently empty index.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; two-strikes pivot to unconditional rebuild
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer; must specifically check that an empty index is not reported as OK
work_units.tests_required: corrupted-cache test (truncated, zero-byte, wrong-schema); each must rebuild, and an EMPTY rebuilt index must be treated as a failure not a success.
work_units.title: Index staleness invalidation keyed on content hash

work_units.evidence_requirement: Recorded terminal transcript of three dry runs including one no-fit query, showing exit code 0 and structured output on stdout.
work_units.question_or_target: Ship an ast route CLI that answers, for an arbitrary query string, exactly what the router would select, with confidence, explanation and near-misses - WITHOUT injecting anything. Exact target: an owner can audit routing behavior without starting a session.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer runs only the documented examples, nothing else
work_units.tests_required: CLI contract test: documented flags all parse; a documented example in the help text is executed verbatim by the test (documentation command test).
work_units.title: Owner-facing route dry-run CLI

work_units.evidence_requirement: A forced-exception run: router patched to raise, full session smoke passes, hook exit codes all 0, zero exit-2 events in the hook log.
work_units.question_or_target: Wire the router into the harness hook surface (prompt-submit and pre-tool) so injection is additive-only and any router error exits 0. Exact question: with the router forced to raise on every call, does the session still function normally with zero blocked tools?
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; a hook that can block is an availability risk - escalate
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus a security reviewer confirming no new block path was introduced
work_units.tests_required: fail-open test with a forced exception; block-never test asserting the router can never emit exit 2; edit-the-repo-source test asserting the deployed copy was not hand-edited.
work_units.title: Router hook integration contract with guaranteed fail-open

work_units.evidence_requirement: Tombstone table: old id, new id, and a resolution probe result per row; any row resolving to a missing target is a defect, not a note.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement tombstone records so a renamed or retired capability still resolves - the router must follow a redirect rather than returning a dead selection. Exact question: how many redirect tombstones exist in the current trees, and does each one resolve to a live target?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
work_units.tests_required: redirect test on a real tombstone; cycle test asserting a tombstone chain cannot loop; negative control asserting a live capability is never treated as a tombstone.
work_units.title: Capability tombstone and rename-redirect handling

work_units.evidence_requirement: A/B diff of two identical sessions, shadow on and shadow off, showing byte-identical injected context; plus the numeric arming criterion written into the config, not into prose.
work_units.question_or_target: Ship the router in SHADOW mode first: it computes and logs what it WOULD have injected, and injects nothing, until calibration data justifies arming it. Exact target: a documented arming criterion expressed as a number, plus proof that shadow mode has zero effect on session behavior.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; arming the router is an owner decision, not a retry outcome
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus owner sign-off before any transition out of shadow
work_units.tests_required: zero-effect test: shadow mode must not change the injected payload by a single byte. Arming-gate test: with calibration below the criterion, arming must be refused.
work_units.title: Router shadow mode: log the would-be selection without injecting

work_units.evidence_requirement: Three-column reconciliation: on-disk state count, process-table count, and registry count, with every disagreement named. A probe whose own command line matches its search pattern must be excluded and that exclusion demonstrated.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement session discovery that enumerates every live agent session from on-disk state (Claude projects transcripts, Codex thread state) into one session registry with vendor, session id, cwd and start time. Exact question: how many sessions does each vendor's own state directory report, and do the two enumerations disagree with the process table?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s; two-strikes pivot to a single-source registry with a declared blind spot
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-enumerates from a mechanically different source (process table vs state files)
work_units.tests_required: self-match control: the discovery probe must not report itself as a session (the CreationDate-equals-probe-runtime tell). Known-present control: a session started 60s earlier must appear.
work_units.title: Session discovery across Claude and Codex on-disk state

work_units.evidence_requirement: Measured CPU delta over a 20s window plus byte growth for one live and one long-finished session; the two cases must produce different verdicts from the same code path.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement liveness as an AND-gate of at least two mechanically independent signals (process CPU delta AND artifact byte-growth), and make mtime-only liveness unrepresentable in the API. Exact target: a long-finished session and a stalled session must be distinguishable, or the API must refuse to answer.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; a wrong liveness verdict authorizes a kill - escalate
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter; must try to make the detector report a finished session as stalled
work_units.tests_required: both-states test: the liveness call must return ALIVE for a running fixture and NOT-ALIVE for a finished one. A stalled-versus-finished case must return UNDECIDABLE rather than guessing.
work_units.title: Two-signal session liveness with an explicit no-mtime rule

work_units.evidence_requirement: Concurrency run output: 50 attempts, exactly 1 grant, 49 typed DENIED results with reason codes. Raw counts, not a summary sentence.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement claim acquire, renew and release for a work unit using atomic tmp-plus-rename with a TTL, so two sessions can never both hold the same unit. Exact question: under 50 concurrent acquire attempts on one unit id, how many claims are granted?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; a second double-grant is a design failure - redesign, do not retry
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-codex-reviewer, fresh context, re-runs the concurrency test
work_units.tests_required: concurrency test at N=50; crash test where the holder is killed mid-claim and the TTL must eventually release it; a mutation removing the atomic rename must turn the concurrency test red.
work_units.title: Crash-safe work-claim protocol with TTL

work_units.evidence_requirement: Event log excerpt showing a non-holder write producing a conflict event, and the same write still succeeding (advisory, not blocking).
work_units.question_or_target: Implement path leases so a session can declare the files it will write, renew while working, and release on exit. Exact target: a lease must be advisory and never block a write, but every write to a leased path by a non-holder must produce a logged conflict event.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
work_units.tests_required: expiry test; renew-extends test; advisory test asserting no write is ever refused; negative control asserting an unleased path produces no conflict event.
work_units.title: Advisory file-lease manager with renew and expiry

work_units.evidence_requirement: Truth table over a 40-pair corpus including 10 case-only-differing pairs and 8 glob-versus-literal pairs, with the algorithm's verdict and the hand-verified answer side by side.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the exact algorithm that decides whether two lease path-sets overlap, including glob patterns, case-insensitive Windows paths, and directory-versus-file containment. Exact target: this is a set-membership question - write the algorithm, do not ask a model to judge it.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; escalate rather than special-casing failures
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer recomputes the 40-pair truth table by an independent method
work_units.tests_required: property test: overlap is symmetric and reflexive; a case-only-differing pair on Windows must overlap; a mutation making the comparison case-sensitive must turn the test red.
work_units.title: Glob-aware pairwise lease-overlap algorithm

work_units.evidence_requirement: Collision list with both unit ids and the shared fingerprint, plus a manual adjudication column; false-positive rate stated with its denominator.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement a fingerprint over the normalized work-unit target text plus its input set, so the same mechanism dispatched twice under different ids is caught at claim time. Exact question: applied to the assembled 2048-unit catalog, how many pairs collide, and is each collision a genuine duplicate or a false positive?
work_units.retry_policy: max 3 attempts for batch transients; zero retries on a report that flags everything
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer adjudicates a random sample of 20 collisions blind
work_units.tests_required: planted-duplicate control: inject one exact duplicate and one reworded duplicate; both must be caught. Planted-distinct control: two genuinely different units with similar vocabulary must NOT collide.
work_units.title: Duplicate-work suppression by normalized unit fingerprint

work_units.evidence_requirement: Per-release record naming both liveness signals and their values; a release with only one signal recorded is a defect.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the reaper that releases claims and leases held by dead sessions, gated on the two-signal liveness AND-gate. Exact target: the reaper must never release a claim held by a live-but-slow session, and must state which two signals it used for each release.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; a wrong reap destroys a peer session's work
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter plus a claude correctness reviewer; both must PASS
work_units.tests_required: live-but-idle test: a session with zero file writes for 20 minutes but a live process must NOT be reaped. Dead-session test: must be reaped. Mutation removing one signal must turn the live-but-idle test red.
work_units.title: Orphan claim and lease reaper gated on proof of death

work_units.evidence_requirement: A rejected-raw-string trace showing the typed boundary refusing an untyped payload, and an accepted handoff showing the goal re-anchored as section 1.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the structured handoff artifact - goal re-anchored at the top, typed sections, evidence anchors - and make raw upstream output physically unable to become the next agent's prefix context. Exact target: the handoff API must accept only typed sections; a raw string must be rejected at the boundary.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
work_units.tests_required: boundary test: passing a raw transcript must raise. Section-completeness test: a handoff missing the re-anchored goal must fail validation.
work_units.title: Typed handoff record replacing raw-output prefix passing

work_units.evidence_requirement: A twelve-row condition table mapping each spec condition to the exact function and line that evaluates it; any condition with no implementing line is a gap, disclosed inline.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the ONE shared completion reducer covering all twelve conditions at spec lines 10631-10644 as a single importable library with no per-caller variants. Exact target: exit code zero alone must be structurally incapable of returning COMPLETE.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; the reducer is the program's single point of epistemic failure
work_units.reviewer_requirement: 2 independent reviewers: correctness plus an adversarial refuter attempting to construct a false COMPLETE
work_units.tests_required: exit-zero-alone test must return INCOMPLETE. Each of the twelve conditions gets one violating fixture that must be rejected.
work_units.title: Shared completion predicate implemented once as a library

work_units.evidence_requirement: Twelve-row results table: condition, fixture path, reducer verdict. Any ACCEPT row names the unenforced condition explicitly.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the generator that synthesizes, for each of the twelve completion conditions, an artifact that violates exactly that one condition and satisfies the other eleven. Exact question: does the reducer reject all twelve, and for any it accepts, which condition is unenforced?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; a reducer that rejects the positive control is a broken detector - fix before re-running
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter who defaults to REFUTED
work_units.tests_required: generator control: the all-conditions-satisfied fixture must be ACCEPTED, proving the generator can produce a passing artifact and the reducer is not simply rejecting everything.
work_units.title: Negative-control fixture generator for the completion reducer

work_units.evidence_requirement: Before and after census counts from a grep over the tree, with every surviving non-library check listed by file:line and justified or removed.
work_units.question_or_target: Replace every local completion check at the seven call sites the spec names (local runner, cloud dispatcher, monitor, harvester, workflow fan-in, cross-vendor adapter, final synthesis) with the shared library, and emit a census proving no site retains its own predicate. Exact question: how many independent completion checks exist in the tree before and after?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-runs the census with a different pattern
work_units.tests_required: import-graph test asserting all seven sites import the shared library; a planted local predicate must be caught by the census (detector control).
work_units.title: Reducer call-site adoption and census across all seven fan-in points

work_units.evidence_requirement: Disagreement matrix across all call-site pairs over 200 artifacts; zero disagreements required, and the corpus must contain at least 40 borderline artifacts or the oracle is too easy.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the differential oracle for spec failure class 'two completion predicates disagree' at line 11314: run every call site against one shared artifact corpus and assert byte-identical verdicts. Exact question: on a 200-artifact corpus, do any two call sites disagree on even one artifact?
work_units.retry_policy: max 3 attempts for batch transients only
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-codex-reviewer re-runs the oracle including the planted divergence
work_units.tests_required: planted-divergence control: patch one call site to use a laxer threshold; the oracle must fire. If it does not, the oracle measures nothing.
work_units.title: Two-predicates-disagree differential oracle

work_units.evidence_requirement: A side-by-side capability matrix with one row per capability and a VENDOR-ONLY marker; the intersection must be computed, not asserted.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement capability negotiation: each vendor adapter publishes a typed descriptor (available tools, context window, permission model, streaming support, schema support) and the dispatcher computes the negotiated common subset for a cross-vendor unit. Exact question: what capability does each vendor have that the other does not, and what does the intersection cost the unit?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus a cross-vendor codex reviewer confirming the codex column is accurate
work_units.tests_required: negotiation test: a unit requiring a vendor-only capability must be refused for the other vendor, not silently downgraded.
work_units.title: Vendor capability descriptor and negotiated common subset

work_units.evidence_requirement: A dispatch trace where a unit declaring read-only permissions attempts a write and is refused by the adapter, with the refusal recorded.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the Claude adapter that takes a catalog work unit and executes it as a subagent with the unit's declared tool_permissions and timeout, returning a typed result. Exact target: the adapter must enforce the unit's tool_permissions at dispatch, not merely document them.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s; escalate on any permission bypass
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus a security reviewer on the permission enforcement path
work_units.tests_required: permission-boundary test per permission class; timeout test asserting the declared timeout is the one applied, not a default.
work_units.title: Anthropic-side work-unit adapter (synchronous, typed)

work_units.evidence_requirement: Recorded invocation showing the prompt file path on the command line (not the prompt body), the exit code, AND the non-empty parsed output-last-message file. Exit code alone is SEVERED, not SUCCESS.
work_units.failure_classification: P0-blocking / classes: severed-stream, fire-and-forget, win-arg-limit, codex-exit-n, schema-invalid
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the Codex adapter: blocking foreground invocation, prompt delivered by FILE not inline, --ignore-user-config, and an explicit output-last-message file. Exact target: a work-unit dispatch must be structurally unable to run detached, because a detached result is unreachable by the fan-in barrier.
work_units.retry_policy: max 1 retry ONLY on a win-arg-limit classification, re-invoked with --ignore-user-config; all other failures escalate immediately
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-codex-reviewer, fresh context; must confirm the three-signal AND-gate
work_units.tests_required: AND-gate test: exit 0 with a missing or empty output file must classify as severed-stream, not success. Detached-invocation test: any attempt to background must raise at the API boundary.
work_units.title: OpenAI-side work-unit adapter with prompt-by-file transport

work_units.evidence_requirement: A generated register from a real dispatch of the same unit through both adapters, with the per-field honored/leaked column filled by the adapters, not by an author.
work_units.question_or_target: Make each adapter emit, at runtime, the list of unit fields it could NOT honor for this vendor - the abstraction leaks - into a machine-readable register. Exact target: the leak register must be produced by the adapter itself, so it cannot drift from the code the way a hand-written compatibility document does.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer compares the generated register against a hand audit of 5 fields
work_units.tests_required: drift test: adding a new unit field neither adapter supports must appear in the register automatically without any documentation edit.
work_units.title: Adapter-emitted abstraction-leak register

work_units.evidence_requirement: A forced-mismatch dispatch showing the DEGRADED verdict, the preserved partial artifact path, and its byte size.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the degrade-loudly contract at spec line 10983: on a capability mismatch the dispatcher returns a typed DEGRADED result and PRESERVES the partial artifact, never a silent substitution and never a discard. Exact target: there must be no code path where a mismatch produces an ordinary-looking success.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; retrying a capability mismatch cannot fix it
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter; must attempt to produce a silent success from a mismatch
work_units.tests_required: mismatch test asserting DEGRADED not SUCCESS; artifact-preservation test asserting the partial file still exists after the failure; a mutation that discards the partial must turn the test red.
work_units.title: Degrade-loudly contract for capability mismatch

work_units.evidence_requirement: A measured failure curve: payload lengths tried, the exact length at which the spawn errors, and the error text. The threshold must be justified by that measurement, not by a remembered constant.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the guard for spec failure class 'command-line length overflow' at line 11311: measure the marshalled command length before spawn and route to a file-based transport above a safe threshold. Exact question: what is the measured payload length at which this box's CreateProcess actually fails, and is the configured threshold below it?
work_units.retry_policy: max 1 retry with the file transport; no third attempt inline
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-measures the failure length independently
work_units.tests_required: over-threshold test asserting automatic file-transport fallback; under-threshold test asserting inline transport is still used (both-states).
work_units.title: Windows command-line length guard for cross-process dispatch

work_units.evidence_requirement: Gate run over a corpus of real historical results containing at least 3 known receipt-shaped payloads; all 3 rejected, and a matched set of genuine results all accepted.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the fan-in gate that rejects any work result whose payload is a job receipt rather than a result - matching background-start and check-status phrasings - and classifies it as FAILED rather than accepting it. Exact target: a receipt string must never be able to satisfy a barrier.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter; must construct a false positive and a false negative
work_units.tests_required: use-vs-mention control: a legitimate result that DISCUSSES background execution as its subject matter must be ACCEPTED; only a payload whose semantic role is a receipt is rejected. A gate that rejects both is a use-vs-mention defect.
work_units.title: Fire-and-forget receipt rejection gate at the fan-in barrier

work_units.evidence_requirement: One dispatch with MCP active and one with --ignore-user-config, both with a typed schema, with the observed outcome of each recorded verbatim.
work_units.question_or_target: Enforce each unit's declared output_schema on the returned payload at the adapter boundary, before the result reaches any consumer. Exact question: with typed schemas active alongside an MCP inventory, does the typed-output path still function, or does it hit the known typed-schema-times-active-MCP interaction?
work_units.retry_policy: zero retries on schema-invalid; max 1 retry with --ignore-user-config if the failure is the MCP interaction
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-codex-reviewer, fresh context
work_units.tests_required: schema-invalid payload must be classified schema-invalid and NOT retried; valid payload must pass. Both-states control on the MCP-active interaction.
work_units.title: Per-unit output-schema validation at the vendor boundary

work_units.evidence_requirement: Two runs at identical total unit count: burst versus staggered, with observed 429 counts for each. A run with zero 429s in BOTH arms proves nothing and must be re-run at higher load.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement staggered dispatch with a token-bucket arrival rate and provider-side backoff, so quota and arrival rate are scheduler inputs rather than retry outcomes. Exact target: reproduce a 429 storm under a naive burst and show it does not occur under the scheduler, at the same total unit count.
work_units.retry_policy: max 3 attempts for provider 429/529 transients only; never reduce concurrency permanently in response to a provider-side 529
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer; must confirm the burst arm was a real control
