work_units.tests_required: token-bucket unit tests; a both-states control proving the burst arm actually produces 429s, otherwise the comparison is vacuous.
work_units.title: Arrival-rate scheduler treating quota as a scheduler input

work_units.evidence_requirement: A staged-set-versus-declared-scope diff from a run with a sibling agent actively writing; any path outside the declared scope must be listed.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the guard for concurrent agents sharing one git index: forbid broad staging, require a scoped path list, and verify the staged set against the unit's declared file scope before any commit is offered. Exact question: does a scoped stage plus a diff --cached check catch a sibling file that a broad add would have swept in?
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; a contaminated stage must be surfaced to the orchestrator, never auto-corrected
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus a security reviewer on the refusal path
work_units.tests_required: contamination test: with a planted sibling edit present, a broad add must be refused and a scoped add must exclude it. Negative control: a clean tree produces an empty out-of-scope list.
work_units.title: Shared git-index contamination guard for concurrent sessions

work_units.evidence_requirement: Line count and per-line JSON parse result after the 8x500 concurrency run: 4000 lines, 4000 parses, zero interleaved records.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the append-only EVENTS.jsonl writer that is safe under concurrent appends from multiple sessions on Windows. Exact question: under 8 concurrent writers emitting 500 events each, are all 4000 lines present and is any line interleaved or truncated?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; a torn line on the second run is a design failure
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-codex-reviewer re-runs the concurrency test on a cold file
work_units.tests_required: concurrency test at 8x500; a mutation removing the atomic-append mode must produce torn lines and turn the test red.
work_units.title: Concurrent-append event writer for the program event log

work_units.evidence_requirement: Per-store table: store, key shape, repo source file:line, deployed copy file:line. A store armed in the repo but absent from the live tree is still live for anyone who deploys - it must be listed, not dismissed.
work_units.question_or_target: Audit and fix every piece of harness state that must be SESSION-keyed rather than PROJECT-keyed - goal injection, ledger replay, claims, caches - because a project-keyed key bleeds one session's goal into a concurrent sibling. Exact question: which state stores are currently project-keyed, checked in the REPO source and not only in the deployed copy?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer repeats the audit against the repo source specifically
work_units.tests_required: bleed test: two concurrent fixture sessions in the same project must not read each other's goal. Repo-versus-live control asserting the audit read BOTH.
work_units.title: Session-scoped state keying audit against goal bleed

work_units.evidence_requirement: Before and after artifact counts plus total bytes for a real harvest; and one deliberately empty harvest showing the FAILED classification.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the postcondition for spec failure class 'remote harvest silently does nothing' at line 11319: a harvest run must assert a nonzero delta in harvested artifacts, or terminate as FAILED. Exact target: a harvest that returns exit 0 having transferred nothing must be classified FAILED, not SUCCESS.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s; escalate if the second harvest is also empty
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
work_units.tests_required: empty-harvest test must FAIL the run; nonempty-harvest test must pass. A harvester that passes both is not discriminating.
work_units.title: Remote-harvest postcondition proving the harvest did something

work_units.evidence_requirement: Per-worktree table: path, resolved origin URL, match verdict. Includes at least one deliberately wrong-repo path proving the guard refuses it.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the guard for spec failure class 'worktree points to the wrong repository' at line 11321: before any file write in a worktree, assert the resolved origin remote URL matches the pinned program repo. Exact target: a write into a worktree owned by a different repository must be impossible, not merely discouraged.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; a wrong-repo write can destroy another session's work
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus a security reviewer; both must PASS before this guard is relied on
work_units.tests_required: wrong-repo test must refuse the write; right-repo test must permit it (both-states). A worktree with no origin must be refused, not defaulted to allowed.
work_units.title: Worktree-target repository assertion before any write

work_units.evidence_requirement: Proof the referenced path was absent before this unit (directory listing) and present after; plus a validation pass over one synthetic receipt per catalog unit shape.
work_units.question_or_target: Author command-center/schema/receipt.schema.json - the file that defaults.output_schema in WORK-UNIT-CATALOG.json already points at and that does not exist on disk. Exact target: a schema strict enough that a receipt missing its sentinel, its evidence anchors, or its reviewer verdict is INVALID, and permissive enough that all 103 existing catalog units can satisfy it.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; a second schema that admits an empty receipt is a design failure, escalate to the contracts bucket
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus a cross-vendor codex reviewer on strictness; both must PASS
work_units.tests_required: schema self-validation against its metaschema; twelve negative fixtures (one per completion condition) that must all be INVALID; one positive fixture that must be VALID.
work_units.title: Author the absent receipt schema every work unit is contracted to satisfy

work_units.evidence_requirement: Round-trip proof: write a receipt, read it back from disk, parse it, and validate it - with the on-disk byte count reported. A path printed in prose is not proof the file exists.
work_units.question_or_target: Create command-center/receipts/ and implement the atomic writer (tmp plus rename) that every work unit uses to emit its receipt. Exact question: all 103 existing catalog output_path values point into a directory that does not exist - after this unit, can a unit actually emit a schema-valid receipt, verified by writing one and reading it back?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer performs the read-back independently
work_units.tests_required: atomicity test: a writer killed mid-write must leave either the old file or nothing, never a half-file. Read-back test asserting the parsed content equals what was written.
work_units.title: Receipts directory and atomic receipt writer library

work_units.evidence_requirement: Both-states CI evidence: the gate red on a deliberately invalid receipt and green on a valid one, with the run ids and the failing step name for the red run.
work_units.question_or_target: Ship the receipt validator as a command and wire it into the existing command-center CI gate so an invalid or missing receipt turns the gate red. Exact question: with a deliberately invalid receipt committed, does the gate actually fail, or does it pass because the validator is invoked in a mode where the check is a no-op?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer confirms the red run failed at the validator step and not elsewhere
work_units.tests_required: both-states gate test; a no-op-mode test asserting the validator cannot be invoked in a mode where it validates nothing.
work_units.title: Receipt validator command wired into the command-center CI gate

work_units.evidence_requirement: A resolved-view dump for three units - one taking all defaults, one overriding three fields, one overriding all nine - showing the effective value and its provenance (default or override) per field.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement per-unit override support in WORK-UNIT-CATALOG.json for the nine mandatory fields that today exist only in a single global defaults block with zero of 103 items overriding them (assignment, tool_permissions, execution_substrate, timeout_seconds, output_schema, tests_required, reviewer_requirement, retry_policy, failure_classification). Exact question: what is the precedence rule when a unit sets a field the defaults block also sets, and is it enforced by code or only described?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; escalate to the owner-decision queue if the intent (deliberate scoping versus gap) is unresolved after 2
work_units.reviewer_requirement: 2 independent reviewers: a schema reviewer and an adversarial refuter probing the null semantics
work_units.tests_required: precedence test per field; a unit-level null must mean explicit-null, not fall-through-to-default; a mutation deleting the defaults block must be caught rather than silently leaving nine fields unset.
work_units.title: Per-unit override semantics for the nine globally-defaulted catalog fields

work_units.evidence_requirement: Before: the defaults-block-deleted mutation exits 0. After: the same mutation exits nonzero. Both exit codes recorded verbatim from the same command line.
work_units.question_or_target: Arm tools/command-center/validate.py field completeness: require_complete defaults to False and CI invokes the tool bare, so deleting the ENTIRE defaults block exits 0 and passes the gate. Exact target: after this unit, that same deletion must turn CI red.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer reproduces both the before and after exit codes
work_units.tests_required: the defaults-deletion mutation is the test; it must fail the gate. A second control mutation (delete one field only) must also fail.
work_units.title: Arm the disarmed work-unit field-completeness check in CI

work_units.evidence_requirement: Sixteen-row table: mutation, pre-fix result, post-fix result. The surviving mutation must be named and its unprotected behavior described before the fix is written.
work_units.question_or_target: Extend the validate.py mutation battery to cover every check the tool claims, and close the one mutation in sixteen that currently SURVIVES. Exact question: which check is unprotected, and after the fix does the full battery reach sixteen of sixteen caught?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; if the seventeenth mutation also survives, expand the battery rather than declaring done
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter designs a seventeenth mutation the battery has never seen
work_units.tests_required: the battery is the test; a control mutation known to be caught must remain caught after the fix (no regression in detection).
work_units.title: Complete the validate.py mutation battery and close the surviving mutation

work_units.evidence_requirement: Per-file digest table with three columns - working-tree hash, blob hash, recorded provenance hash - across all fourteen manifest entries, taken on a Windows checkout.
work_units.question_or_target: Fix the command-center provenance check so it hashes the COMMITTED blob rather than working-tree bytes, making it runnable on a Windows checkout where core.autocrlf rewrites line endings. Exact question: after the fix, do the Windows and Linux runs produce the same digest for all fourteen manifest entries?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-derives two digests by a different command than the implementation uses
work_units.tests_required: platform-parity test asserting the blob route yields identical digests on a CRLF and an LF checkout; a control asserting the working-tree route DIFFERS, proving the fix changed something.
work_units.title: Make the provenance hash read the committed blob, not the working tree

work_units.evidence_requirement: Three-route byte comparison on one file (archive+extract, cat-file, show) with byte counts and CRLF counts, plus a control proving all three are identical after LF normalization so the difference is purely line endings; then the grep census of remaining wrong-recipe call sites, which must be zero.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement ONE blob_bytes(rev, path) helper on git cat-file, route every provenance, formatting and parity path through it, and remove every use of the archive-plus-extract recipe - which returns export-converted CRLF on this box, the OPPOSITE of the blob. Exact question: how many call sites and documents currently prescribe the wrong recipe, and are all of them corrected?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-measures the three-route comparison on a DIFFERENT file
work_units.tests_required: helper unit test on a known file; a repo-wide grep test asserting zero archive-based provenance recipes remain (detector control: plant one and confirm the grep finds it).
work_units.title: Single blob-bytes helper and removal of the archive-based recipe everywhere

work_units.evidence_requirement: Exit codes of both gates on the Windows working tree before and after, plus confirmation that the Linux CI run stayed green across the change (a fix that greens Windows by reddening CI is a regression).
work_units.question_or_target: Add the EOL attributes that make the command-center gates runnable on the primary development box, then prove both gates exit zero on a Windows working tree. Exact target: the machine the program is authored on must be able to run its own gates - today both exit nonzero purely from CRLF while being genuinely green in CI.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; escalate rather than normalizing line endings destructively across the tree
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer runs both gates from a clean re-clone on Windows
work_units.tests_required: dual-platform gate test; a control asserting the pre-fix Windows run really was red, so the after-state is not silence in both states.
work_units.title: EOL policy and a Windows-checkout green-gate proof

work_units.evidence_requirement: A time-series of observed concurrent units per substrate across a 40-unit mixed dry run; the local-serialized series must be flat at one.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the dispatcher that reads the catalog and routes each unit to its declared execution_substrate, with local-serialized meaning strictly one at a time. Exact question: with a catalog containing units of all four substrates, does the observed simultaneous count for local-serialized ever exceed one?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer inspects the time-series, not the summary
work_units.tests_required: substrate-isolation test per substrate; a mutation removing the serial lock must show a concurrent count above one and turn the test red.
work_units.title: Work-unit dispatcher honoring the declared execution substrate

work_units.evidence_requirement: Kill-and-resume trace with executed-unit multiset before and after; any unit appearing twice is a defect and must be listed.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the append-only run ledger so an interrupted program resumes without re-running completed units and without double-counting. Exact question: after killing the runner at 60 percent and resuming, is the total set of executed units exactly the catalog with no unit executed twice?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; a duplicate execution on the second attempt is a design failure
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-codex-reviewer reproduces one kill-and-resume cycle
work_units.tests_required: idempotent-replay property test; kill-at-N test for N in {10,50,90} percent; a mutation making replay non-idempotent must produce duplicates and turn the test red.
work_units.title: Resumable run-state ledger with idempotent replay

work_units.evidence_requirement: Peak observed simultaneity per substrate over a simulated 2048-unit schedule, sampled at 1Hz, against the configured ceiling.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the governor enforcing spec line 10570 - do not launch all units simultaneously - with per-substrate ceilings, staggered arrivals, and a live simultaneous-count readout. Exact target: a 2048-unit catalog must be schedulable without the simultaneous count ever exceeding the configured per-substrate ceiling.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer confirms the readout is measured, not derived from the ceiling constant
work_units.tests_required: ceiling-hold test under a burst arrival pattern; a mutation raising a ceiling must be visible in the readout (the readout must not be computed from the config it is meant to check).
work_units.title: Concurrency governor separating logical unit count from simultaneity

work_units.evidence_requirement: A recorded approach-to-ceiling run showing the commit counter rising, the guard firing, and a process spawn still succeeding after it fired. RAM-percent alone is NOT the signal and must be shown to be uninformative here.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the local-headroom guard that refuses to raise concurrency when the machine is near its commit-charge ceiling - the measured cause of full-box freezes, which is invisible in ordinary RAM readings. Exact question: which counter does the guard read, and does it fire before the box loses the ability to create a process?
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; never respond to this guard by killing a shared service
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus owner sign-off, because this guard throttles the owner's own machine
work_units.tests_required: threshold test with a synthetic commit-charge reading; a control proving RAM-percent alone would not have fired, so the guard is measuring the right counter.
work_units.title: Commit-charge headroom guard preserving a rescue shell

work_units.evidence_requirement: For each teardown candidate: the preservation proof used (merged-PR state or content digest match) and the ancestry reading, shown side by side to demonstrate ancestry alone would have given the wrong answer at least once.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement disposable worktree provisioning per implementation shard (spec line 10581) and a teardown that refuses to delete until the shard's content is proven preserved elsewhere. Exact target: because squash-merge makes a fully-merged branch report as AHEAD, commit ancestry must NOT be accepted as delete authorization - require merged-PR state or a byte-level content comparison.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; an incorrect teardown is unrecoverable data loss
work_units.reviewer_requirement: 2 independent reviewers plus owner approval before any real teardown
work_units.tests_required: squash-merge fixture: a fully-merged branch reporting AHEAD must still be judged safe by the content route and unsafe by the ancestry route. Teardown must refuse when neither proof is available.
work_units.title: Worktree-per-shard provisioner with content-preserving teardown

work_units.evidence_requirement: Time-to-classification for a hung fixture, with both signals recorded (no heartbeat AND no byte growth). A single-signal STALLED verdict is a defect.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement per-unit timeout and hang detection with a heartbeat, so a unit that stops producing output is classified STALLED and released rather than silently occupying a slot. Exact question: for a deliberately hung unit, how long until the runner classifies it, and does the classification require two signals?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter attempts to make a live slow unit be classified stalled
work_units.tests_required: hung-unit test; slow-but-alive test that must NOT be classified stalled; mutation removing the byte-growth signal must make the slow-but-alive test red.
work_units.title: Per-unit timeout enforcement with heartbeat hang detection

work_units.evidence_requirement: Decision table: failure class, configured policy, observed attempt count. Any class whose observed count differs from its policy is a defect.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the retry engine so the retry decision is a pure function of the typed failure class, not of the raw error text. Exact target: a schema-invalid failure must be retried ZERO times, a provider transient up to its cap, and a second failure on the same fingerprint must trigger the two-strikes pivot rather than a third attempt.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts to implement; the engine must not be able to retry its own failure indefinitely
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
work_units.tests_required: one test per failure class; a same-fingerprint repeat test asserting the pivot fires at strike two, not strike three.
work_units.title: Retry-policy engine driven by typed failure classification

work_units.evidence_requirement: Coverage table mapping each of the taxonomy classes to at least one real observed error string from the corpus; any class with no real example is speculative and must be labelled as such.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the closed failure taxonomy (severed-stream, adapter-exit-n, win-arg-limit, timeout, schema-invalid, partial-artifact, degraded, blocked) and a formatter that emits every tool result as an explicit terminal state. Exact target: an open-ended prose result must be structurally impossible; every result carries SUCCESS with an id or FAILED with an id and a reason.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus a cross-vendor codex reviewer supplying codex-side error strings
work_units.tests_required: exhaustiveness test: an unclassifiable error must map to an explicit UNCLASSIFIED terminal state, never to a silent success or an empty return.
work_units.title: Failure taxonomy and terminal-state result formatter

work_units.evidence_requirement: A control-plane census before and after (count of independent state-mutating surfaces), plus a rendered screenshot or captured pane output proving the new pane displays live data.
work_units.question_or_target: Extend the EXISTING monitor cockpit with a program pane reading EVENTS.jsonl and receipts read-only - explicitly NOT a new control plane, per spec line 10483. Exact question: after this unit, how many distinct control planes exist for program state, and is the answer one?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus an architecture reviewer on the duplicate-control-plane question
work_units.tests_required: read-only test asserting the pane cannot mutate program state; a census test asserting no second dispatcher was introduced.
work_units.title: Cockpit surface extending the existing monitor rather than a second control plane

work_units.evidence_requirement: Four-cell truth table (monitor alive/dead x work active/idle) with the detector verdict in each cell; any cell where the detector guesses instead of returning UNDECIDABLE is a defect.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement both detectors from spec lines 11315-11316 together: a monitor that dies while remote work continues, and a live monitor that merely has nothing to report being mistaken for dead. Exact target: the two states must be distinguishable, and where they are not, the detector must return UNDECIDABLE rather than guessing.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter constructs the hardest cell
work_units.tests_required: all four cells as tests; a mutation collapsing the two signals into one must make two cells indistinguishable and turn the test red.
work_units.title: Stale-monitor and no-change-monitor detectors as a matched pair

work_units.evidence_requirement: Terminal-state count for the 40-unit batch with one hung unit: 39 terminal plus 1 STALLED, with wall-clock time to completion of the 39.
work_units.question_or_target: Replace phase-wide barriers with per-unit pipelines so a single hung unit cannot deadlock its cohort (spec line 11317). Exact question: with one unit deliberately hung forever in a 40-unit batch, do the other 39 still reach a terminal state?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-runs the 40-unit batch
work_units.tests_required: hung-unit-in-batch test; a null-tolerant fan-in test asserting a null result from one unit does not poison the barrier for the rest.
work_units.title: Per-unit pipeline so one hung unit cannot block a batch

work_units.evidence_requirement: A killed-late fixture run showing the partial file still on disk with its byte size, classified INCOMPLETE, and referenced from the run ledger.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement handling for spec line 11313 - an artifact that exists but carries no sentinel is INCOMPLETE, must be PRESERVED, and must never be deleted or reported as success. Exact target: a partial artifact must survive the failure that produced it, so a long unit that dies late is recoverable.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
work_units.tests_required: kill-late test asserting the file survives; a mutation that cleans up partials on failure must turn the test red. Negative control: a complete artifact must not be classified INCOMPLETE.
work_units.title: Partial-artifact preservation and INCOMPLETE classification

work_units.evidence_requirement: Set difference between artifacts on disk and manifest entries after a full run; must be the empty set, computed mechanically.
work_units.question_or_target: Wire artifact-manifest registration into the writer so completion condition 11 (output registered in the artifact manifest) is satisfied by construction rather than by a later sweep. Exact question: can any artifact reach disk without a manifest entry, and what is the count of unregistered artifacts after a full run?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer recomputes the set difference
work_units.tests_required: bypass test: an artifact written by a direct file open (not the writer) must be caught by the reconciliation sweep as unregistered.
work_units.title: Automatic artifact-manifest registration at emit time

work_units.evidence_requirement: Probe output for three fixtures: readable, exists-but-unparseable, and parseable-but-missing-required-field. The third must FAIL, or the probe measures existence rather than readability.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the probe for completion condition 12 - downstream consumers can read it - by having a real consumer open, parse and extract a required field from the artifact, not merely stat it. Exact target: existence is not readability; the probe must fail on a file that exists, parses, but lacks the field the consumer needs.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter constructs a fourth fixture that passes the probe but breaks a real consumer
work_units.tests_required: three-fixture test as above; a mutation reducing the probe to os.path.exists must turn the third fixture green and thereby red the test.
work_units.title: Downstream-readability probe satisfying completion condition twelve

work_units.evidence_requirement: Merge report: per-slice count, id range, gaps, duplicates, and the total against the declared program count. Any nonzero gap or duplicate blocks the merge.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the merger that assembles the catalog slices from every bucket into one WORK-UNIT-CATALOG.json and refuses on a duplicate id or an unfilled index gap (spec line 11320, duplicate units from colliding catalogs). Exact question: across all assembled slices, are the ids contiguous, unique, and exactly equal to the declared program count?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer recounts each slice independently from the files on disk
work_units.tests_required: planted-duplicate test must block the merge; planted-gap test must block; a clean slice set must merge (positive control, proving the merger is not simply refusing everything).
work_units.title: Catalog slice merge with duplicate-id and mechanism collision detection

work_units.evidence_requirement: All twenty-one stopping conditions evaluated under PR-ONLY with a per-condition verdict of TRUE, FALSE, or NOT-APPLICABLE plus the recorded owner justification for every NOT-APPLICABLE.
work_units.question_or_target: Resolve the measured contradiction that under the binding PR-ONLY release mode, program stopping condition 13 (release or canary succeeds) is permanently unsatisfiable as written. Exact target: implement release-mode-aware evaluation so a condition that cannot apply resolves to an explicitly recorded NOT-APPLICABLE with an owner-visible justification, never to a silent pass and never to a permanent block.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; this changes when the program is allowed to declare itself done
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus explicit owner approval of each NOT-APPLICABLE
work_units.tests_required: mode test: under a canary release mode the same condition must be REQUIRED, not not-applicable (both-states). A NOT-APPLICABLE without a recorded justification must fail validation.
work_units.title: Release-mode adaptation of the program stopping predicate

work_units.evidence_requirement: Scan results over the full corpus with zero-entropy prefixes only (never a secret value), plus a planted-canary run proving the scanner fires on a known-present synthetic credential.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the gate for spec line 11345 - credentials or decrypted secrets entering an artifact bundle - scanning every receipt, event and packaged artifact before it is registered. Exact target: detection and REPORTING only; the gate must name the variable, the scope and the evidence, and must never itself rotate, revoke or unset any credential.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry on a positive finding; escalate to the owner immediately with the blast-radius trace
work_units.reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus an independent claude reviewer; both must PASS, and the no-rotation property must be verified by reading the code, not by testing
work_units.tests_required: canary test (must fire); false-positive control on a document that MENTIONS a credential variable name without containing a value (must NOT fire) - the use-versus-mention distinction; and an assertion that the gate has no code path that modifies a credential.
work_units.title: Secret-scrub gate on the program artifact corpus

work_units.evidence_requirement: Per-field acceptance matrix produced by feeding each candidate field to the real parser one at a time, with the verbatim rejection message for each rejected field.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11302 (strict plugin parser rejects unknown fields). Implement the emission policy so no shipped manifest ever contains a field the strictest supported client rejects, plus a forward-compatibility shim for reading manifests that do. Exact question: which manifest fields does the strictest client currently reject, measured by feeding it each field in isolation?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-runs the per-field matrix
work_units.tests_required: strict-parse test on the emitted manifest; a planted unknown field must be rejected by the test (detector control) and must never reach the emitted artifact.
work_units.title: Strict-parser unknown-field policy for every shipped manifest

work_units.evidence_requirement: Declared-versus-observed hook count with every missing marker named; a config-file listing is explicitly NOT accepted as evidence of loading.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11303 (plugin appears installed but hooks are unloaded). Implement a POSITIVE load probe: each hook emits a load marker the verifier reads, so installed status is never inferred from the presence of a config file. Exact question: how many declared hooks actually emit their load marker at session start, and does that number equal the declared count?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer verifies the broken-state reading specifically
work_units.tests_required: both-states test: a deliberately malformed hook config must produce a LOWER observed count (proving the probe can see the broken state), and the repaired config must restore it. A probe silent in both states measures nothing.
work_units.title: Positive hook-load verification, not installed-status inference

work_units.evidence_requirement: Resolution table showing what each shell reports for the same interpreter name, with the resolved absolute path for each, demonstrating the two shells disagree.
inputs: interpreter discovery results from both shells
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11304 (bare .sh invocation on Windows). Implement a launcher that resolves an explicit interpreter per script type and refuses bare invocation. Exact target: distinguish the MSYS bash from the Windows system bash, because the latter is WSL and mangles Windows paths and rejects CRLF - a resolver that reports only one of them is wrong.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-resolves from the other shell
work_units.tests_required: CRLF script test under the real target interpreter, not under the tolerant one; a bare-invocation attempt must be refused. Both-shell control proving the resolver consulted both.
work_units.title: Explicit interpreter resolution banning bare script invocation

work_units.evidence_requirement: Per-file classification into identical, EOL-only, repo-larger, live-larger, and diverged-both-unique, with counts. A one-directional summary that reports only which side is ahead is exactly the defect and is not acceptable evidence.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11305 (repository copy differs from live deployed copy). Implement the synchronizer so it REFUSES a one-directional copy whenever both sides hold unique content. Exact question: for the currently diverged rule tree, how many files differ in real content versus by line endings only, and how many are larger on each side?
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; a one-directional sync over diverged content destroys the smaller side
work_units.reviewer_requirement: 2 independent reviewers; the classification must be recomputed by a second differ
work_units.tests_required: both-unique fixture must be REFUSED; a purely one-directional fixture must be permitted (both-states). Detector control: an EOL-only difference must not be classified as content divergence.
work_units.title: Two-directional divergence refusal in the repo-to-live synchronizer

work_units.evidence_requirement: A publish-then-observe trace with the observed version at each invocation; the fixed content must appear on the first invocation after publish.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11306 (stale cache masks a fixed package). Implement content-addressed package caching plus an explicit refresh command. Exact question: after publishing a fixed package, how many client invocations does it take before the fix is observed, and is that number one?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
work_units.tests_required: stale-cache test: with a cached old package present, the new one must still be observed. Corrupt-cache test must rebuild rather than serve garbage or an empty package.
work_units.title: Package cache invalidation that cannot mask a fixed package

work_units.evidence_requirement: Full packed file list with total bytes, plus the per-pattern match count. A pattern matching zero files across every build is either dead or the detector is broken - it must be named either way.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11307 (package accidentally includes .git or huge unrelated files). Implement the packaging gate that enumerates the exact file list before packing and fails on any excluded path or on exceeding the declared size ceiling. Exact question: what is the packaged artifact size and file count, and which of the exclusion patterns actually matched something?
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry on a credential match; escalate with a blast-radius trace
work_units.reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus an independent claude reviewer; both must PASS
work_units.tests_required: planted .git directory, planted 200MB file, planted credential file - each must fail the gate independently. Clean build must pass (positive control).
work_units.title: Package content gate with an explicit exclusion set and size ceiling

work_units.evidence_requirement: Transport failure matrix over the payload corpus: transport, payload shape, observed outcome. Include at least one payload whose BODY quotes a destructive command, because a payload can be scanned as if it were a command line.
inputs: payload corpus with apostrophes, quotes and control bytes
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11308 (shell quoting corrupts script content). Implement a marshaller that never inlines a payload containing an apostrophe, a here-string terminator, or a control byte - routing all such content through a written file and a path argument. Exact question: at what payload shape does each transport break, measured rather than assumed?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; after the second quoting failure switch transport rather than escaping a third time
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-runs the matrix from the other shell
work_units.tests_required: round-trip integrity test asserting the received bytes equal the sent bytes for every corpus entry; a control payload known to break the naive transport must be shown breaking it.
work_units.title: Quoting-safe command marshaller with file-based payload transport

work_units.evidence_requirement: Both-direction evidence: a revision argument surviving unconverted, AND a legitimate POSIX path argument still being converted correctly under the same configuration. A run showing only one direction is half a proof.
inputs: argument corpus (revisions, device paths, POSIX paths)
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11309 (PowerShell and Git Bash path rewriting). Implement path-conversion suppression that is COMMAND-aware and ARGUMENT-aware: applied around revision-shaped and device-path arguments, never globally, because a global suppression breaks legitimate POSIX path arguments and silently produces a no-op. Exact target: prove both failure directions are prevented, not just one.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus an adversarial refuter on the silent-no-op direction
work_units.tests_required: per-argument-shape test; a global-suppression fixture must FAIL the legitimate-path case, proving the scoped implementation is not equivalent to the global one.
work_units.title: Argument-aware shell path-rewriting control

work_units.evidence_requirement: Enumeration count over the fixture tree with and without the reserved-name file present; the counts must differ by exactly one and neither run may raise.
inputs: fixture tree containing reserved names and a >260 char path
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the path library that handles Windows extended-length paths and reserved device names (NUL, CON, AUX, PRN) without aborting a directory walk. Exact question: does a tree containing a file named NUL still enumerate completely, and what does the relative-path computation return for it?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
work_units.tests_required: reserved-name test; long-path test above 260 characters; a control asserting the walk does NOT silently swallow the exception and return zero entries.
work_units.title: Path library for extended-length paths and reserved device names

work_units.evidence_requirement: Collision list with file, both keys, and the value each holds; a zero result must be accompanied by a planted-collision control proving the detector fires.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11310 (case-insensitive parser collision on case-distinct JSON keys). Implement the detector that finds two keys differing only by case in any shipped config or manifest, before a case-insensitive consumer silently drops one. Exact question: how many such collisions exist across the shipped configuration surface today?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
work_units.tests_required: planted-collision control; nested-object coverage test; a control asserting keys that differ by more than case are not reported.
work_units.title: Case-distinct key collision detector for configuration documents

work_units.evidence_requirement: Three-dot diff stat with files changed and deletions, alongside the two-dot number, showing they differ - the two-dot form folds in working-tree noise and is not the proposal surface.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11322 (stale branch would revert newer work). Implement the guard that measures the three-dot commit-to-commit diff against the integration base before any proposal is offered, and blocks when the surface contains mass deletions the branch did not author. Exact question: how many deletions does this branch propose, and how many of them are files it never touched?
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; a mass-deletion proposal must reach a human
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer recomputes both diff forms
work_units.tests_required: stale-branch fixture must be blocked; a freshly-based branch must pass (both-states). A control asserting the guard reads the three-dot form specifically.
work_units.title: Stale-branch reversion guard on the commit-to-commit surface

work_units.evidence_requirement: Confusion matrix before and after on the historical corpus, with each surviving false positive shown as the raw record so the role-versus-text distinction is visible.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11323 (false-positive prose and fixture detectors). Implement the shared library that classifies a match by its semantic ROLE - the tool-input verb, the JSON field, the AST position - rather than by the presence of a string in the payload, since a document describing a defect necessarily contains that defect's text. Exact question: on the historical false-positive corpus, what is the before-and-after false-positive rate?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter constructs a mention that the library still fires on and a use it misses
work_units.tests_required: mention corpus (documents quoting a dangerous command) must produce zero fires; use corpus (actual invocation) must produce a fire on every entry. A library passing only one of the two corpora is not a fix.
work_units.title: Semantic-role detector library replacing payload-text matching

work_units.evidence_requirement: Per-detector two-state table: broken-state output, good-state output, and a DIFFERS verdict. Every detector with no known-broken fixture is NOT-CHECKED, not passing.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11324 (detector silent in both broken and fixed states). Implement the harness that, for every shipped detector, runs it against a known-BROKEN and a known-GOOD state and requires it to differ. Exact question: how many of the shipped detectors are silent in BOTH states and therefore measure nothing?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter selects three detectors and constructs independent broken states
work_units.tests_required: the harness needs its own control: a detector known to be two-state-valid must be reported valid, and a deliberately inert stub detector must be reported as measuring nothing.
work_units.title: Both-states detector-validation harness applied to every shipped detector

work_units.evidence_requirement: Measured multiplier from the process table (processes divided by sessions), and the configuration scope each server is actually enabled at - a setting present at the wrong scope is inert and must be shown to be inert, not assumed effective.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11326 (eager per-session MCP process multiplication). Implement the guard that measures live child-process count per session and refuses to start a new session tier that would push the machine past its process budget, preferring a shared long-lived service over per-session duplication. Exact question: what is the current processes-per-session multiplier, measured from the process table?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer verifies the effective scope from the process table, not from the config file
work_units.tests_required: scope test asserting the guard reads the scope that actually takes effect; budget test asserting a new tier is refused at the ceiling. Control: the guard must still permit startup below the ceiling.
work_units.title: Per-session process-multiplication guard for MCP-style child processes

work_units.evidence_requirement: A ceiling-pressure run in which a shared service is present and survives, with the guard's per-candidate decision record showing why it was spared.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11328 (kill-based memory guard terminates a live shared service). Implement an allowlist plus a proof-of-orphan requirement so the resource guard can only terminate a process it has proven to be an orphan of a dead session. Exact target: a live shared service must be unkillable by the guard even at the memory ceiling.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; a wrong termination takes down a live service
work_units.reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus owner approval, because this guard can terminate the owner's running services
work_units.tests_required: shared-service-survives test at the ceiling; orphan-is-reaped test; a mutation removing the allowlist must kill the shared service and turn the first test red.
work_units.title: Shared-service protection in the resource guard's termination path

work_units.evidence_requirement: Before-and-after inventories with the computed set difference for both commands and user-data paths; a rollback rehearsal that was never actually executed is NOT-CHECKED, not passing.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11347 (rollback removes existing commands or user data). Implement rollback as an additive-restore with a pre-rollback inventory and a post-rollback diff, so any command or user-data path present before and absent after is a hard failure. Exact question: what is the set difference of available commands and user-data paths across a real rollback, and is it empty?
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry; re-running a destructive rollback compounds the loss
work_units.reviewer_requirement: 2 independent reviewers plus owner approval before rollback is exercised against a real profile
work_units.tests_required: rollback rehearsal on a disposable profile; a planted user-data file must survive; a mutation making rollback destructive must turn the test red.
work_units.title: Rollback contract that cannot remove existing commands or user data

work_units.evidence_requirement: Per-package declared-versus-exercised permission table with the code anchor for each exercised permission; an unexercised grant with no anchor is the finding.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11346 (marketplace package has malicious or excessive permissions). Implement the scanner that compares a package's declared permissions against the minimum its code actually exercises, and flags every grant with no corresponding use. Exact question: for each fixture package, which declared permissions are never exercised by its code?
work_units.retry_policy: max 3 attempts for batch transients; zero retries on a scanner that flags every package
work_units.reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus a cross-vendor codex reviewer on the malicious fixture
work_units.tests_required: malicious fixture package (over-broad grants plus an exfiltration path) must be flagged; a minimal well-scoped package must NOT be flagged (both-states).
work_units.title: Marketplace package permission scanner for excessive and malicious grants

work_units.evidence_requirement: Per-check listing of BOTH probes with their outputs; a check declaring only one probe is a violation and must render as NOT-CHECKED in the report.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the health-check command so every reported status is backed by two mechanically independent probes, and any single-probe check reports NOT-CHECKED rather than OK. Exact question: how many of the health checks can currently produce a green verdict from one probe alone?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer audits three checks for genuine probe independence
work_units.tests_required: single-probe check must render NOT-CHECKED; a two-probe check with disagreeing probes must render DISAGREE, never OK. Positive control on a genuinely healthy component.
work_units.title: Health-check command built on two-signal probes only

work_units.evidence_requirement: A refused in-place edit after the freeze, and an accepted migration with its up and down steps both executed against a fixture corpus.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the migration engine required by spec line 10660 - once the first implementation wave starts, launchers and schemas are frozen and any change requires a versioned migration. Exact target: an in-place schema edit after the freeze marker is set must be refused, and the only accepted path is a numbered migration with an executable down-step.
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer executes the down-step independently
work_units.tests_required: freeze test (in-place edit refused); round-trip test (up then down restores the original bytes); a migration with no down-step must be refused.
work_units.title: Versioned schema migration engine with a launcher freeze marker

work_units.evidence_requirement: Coverage table: taxonomy class, message id, and the next command it recommends. Every recommended command must be executed verbatim by the documentation test.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the user-facing error catalog mapping every class in the failure taxonomy to a message that names what failed, why, and the exact next command. Exact question: how many taxonomy classes currently have no user-facing message, and after this unit is that number zero?
work_units.retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s
work_units.reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer runs three messages end to end as a naive user
work_units.tests_required: coverage test asserting zero unmapped classes; documentation-command test executing every recommended next command; a control asserting a class added later is reported as unmapped.
work_units.title: Actionable error catalog covering every failure class

work_units.evidence_requirement: Canary sweep results across every emission point: planted secret-shaped token, planted absolute home path, planted project name - each must be absent from the emitted stream, with the emission point named.
work_units.question_or_target: Implement the telemetry and privacy contract from spec line 10819: what is recorded, what is redacted, where it is stored, how it is disabled. Exact target: redaction must be proven executably against planted canaries - a policy document is not an implementation, and an ephemeral channel is not exfiltration-safe.
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry on a canary leak; escalate with the blast-radius trace
work_units.reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus owner approval of the recorded-field list
work_units.tests_required: canary test per emission point; opt-out test asserting disabling telemetry emits literally nothing; a control proving the sweep can detect a canary that was NOT redacted.
work_units.title: Telemetry and privacy contract implementation with an executable redaction proof

work_units.evidence_requirement: Behavioral diff for each planted injection: consuming-stage output with and without the injection present. Identical outputs are the pass condition; any divergence names the injection that worked.
work_units.question_or_target: Anchor spec:11344 (an artifact injects instructions into a later stage). Implement the boundary that treats every consumed artifact - transcripts, fetched pages, peer results, participant outputs - as untrusted DATA, never as instructions, with a structural wrapper rather than a prompt-level plea. Exact question: does a planted instruction inside an artifact change the behavior of the consuming stage?
work_units.retry_policy: no automatic retry on a successful injection; escalate and widen the corpus
work_units.reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus an adversarial refuter who authors three new injections the corpus has never seen
work_units.tests_required: injection corpus covering role-spoof, ignore-previous-instructions, encoded payload, and a credential-read request; every one must produce an identical downstream output. Control: a benign artifact edit that SHOULD change the output must change it, proving the diff is sensitive.
work_units.title: Prompt-injection defence on the artifact-consumption boundary

work_units.evidence_requirement: Cite the change-class rule table by file:line and paste the linter exit code for three crafted diffs (one per bump class). A claim that the rule is enforced must cite an exit code, not the presence of the rule in a document.
inputs: the formal contract set produced by the specification lane (B06)
the current plugin manifest and marketplace registry entry
git tags and the tag-to-HEAD diff
work_units.question_or_target: Implementation target: turn the release policy and versioning rules the spec demands at lines 10817-10820 into a machine-checkable artifact. Enumerate, for the plugin package, the registry entry, the blueprint pack and the CouncilSpec schema, exactly which change classes force MAJOR, MINOR or PATCH -- manifest key removal, permission widening, hook-contract signature change, blueprint id retirement, a schema field becoming required -- then ship a linter that derives the REQUIRED bump from the git diff between the previous tag and HEAD and exits non-zero whenever the declared version is lower than the derived one.
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot (AGENTS.md 4b): after the second failure carrying the same error fingerprint, enumerate at least two mechanically different approaches before any third attempt
work_units.reviewer_requirement: one fresh-context adversarial reviewer from the OTHER vendor than this unit's executor; a same-vendor reviewer inherits the executor's blind spots
tests_required: Mutation: delete a required manifest key and declare a PATCH bump -> linter exits non-zero.
Both-states: a genuinely patch-only diff declared as PATCH -> linter silent (no false positive).
Widening a declared tool permission must classify MAJOR even though no key was removed.
A pure file rename with byte-identical content must classify as no-bump-required.
work_units.title: Semantic-version contract with a diff-derived bump linter

work_units.evidence_requirement: The schema file must exist on disk and validate against its own meta-schema; quote the two invariants verbatim with file:line. Every action type must be listed with its inverse or explicitly marked IRREVERSIBLE with an owner-visible impact statement.
inputs: the installer action inventory from the implementation lane (B07)
work_units.question_or_target: Implementation target: write the rollback contract named at spec line 10817 as a typed schema rather than prose. Each action an installer may perform -- write a file, register a hook, add an MCP entry, edit a settings key, create a scheduled task, seed a cache -- must declare its target path or key, whether the pre-existing value is captured first, its inverse action, the invariant that must hold once the inverse has run, and whether the inverse is total or partial. Encode two hard invariants: an inverse may never remove a path the installer did not create, and it may never remove a command, skill or setting that pre-dated the install (spec 11347).
work_units.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot (AGENTS.md 4b): after the second failure carrying the same error fingerprint, enumerate at least two mechanically different approaches before any third attempt
work_units.reviewer_requirement: two reviewers who file independently and do not see each other's verdict until both are filed; disagreement escalates to raw-artifact adjudication, never to a vote
tests_required: An action declared with no inverse and no IRREVERSIBLE marker must fail schema validation.
An inverse whose target lies outside the recorded creation set must fail validation.
A partial inverse must be forced to declare its residue; omitting the residue field must fail.
Positive control: the full real action inventory must validate cleanly, proving the schema is not so strict that nothing conforms.
work_units.title: Rollback contract: every mutating install action declares a typed inverse

work_units.evidence_requirement: The packet must quote spec line 11390 verbatim and cite the PHASE-GRAPH.json field that measured the gap. The answer, once given, must be written to OWNER-DECISIONS.md in the same turn and the receipt must cite the resulting file:line.
inputs: _USER-PROMPTS.md:11364-11370 (how to ask: one question, recommendation, tradeoff, default)
work_units.question_or_target: Question: under the binding PR-ONLY release mode there is no canary channel, so what must succeed in place of program stop condition 13, 'release/canary succeeds' (spec 11390), which currently has no satisfiable referent and therefore makes the program unable to ever meet its own stopping rule? work_units.evidence_requirement: State what the observer can and cannot perceive -- side effects produced by a spawned child process, for instance -- and mark the blind region NOT-CHECKED. inputs: the system-level observer and the measured limits of what it can see
the installer under test, run inside the canary profile

work_units.question_or_target: Implementation target: find out what the recorded recovery plan does NOT cover, by watching the installer run instead of by reading the plan. Attach a system-level observer to a genuine install so each side effect it produces is captured as it happens, then subtract the recorded inverse set from the observed side-effect set in both directions. Anything observed but unrecorded is a recovery hole; anything recorded but never observed is a stale entry that will send the next responder somewhere nothing happened. Coverage inferred from reading a document is not coverage.
work_units.retry_policy: retry only on a FRESH profile. Re-running a lifecycle drill on a dirtied profile measures the dirt, not the drill; the profile must be destroyed and recreated between attempts

Remove a real side effect while leaving its recorded inverse -> the stale-entry direction fires.
Side effects produced by a child process are either captured or declared an uncovered region.
work_units.title: Rollback coverage measured by instrumenting a real install, not by reading the manifest
